title: taskq task spec v1
description: What a submitter asks a worker to run. Immutable once enqueued: its canonical sha256 is bound into every result.

queue.description: Routing class, one per hardware shape (cpu, cpu-exclusive, gpu-sm120). Workers subscribe to queues; there is no scheduler.

kind.description: command: run once. benchmark: warmups + timed repetitions, each measured separately.

repo.description: Alias from the worker's repo allowlist (crypto, crypto-autoresearcher, cryptanalysis). Never a URL.

commit.description: Full commit sha. Branch names are refused: a task must name exactly the code it ran.

sparse_paths.description: Check out only these directories (cone mode) plus top-level files. For large repos: the tree then holds just what the task needs.

cwd.description: Relative to the checkout; may not escape it.

setup.description: Build steps run before argv (e.g. cargo build --release). Timed separately and reported as setup cost, never folded into the measurement.

timeout_seconds.description: Per execution of argv (per repetition for benchmark). Expiry yields status timeout, which is never negative evidence.

require_labels.description: Worker labels that must match exactly (arch, cpu_model, node pool). A worker lacking them hands the task back.

cpus.description: Pin the child to this many CPUs from the worker's affinity set.

max_attempts.description: Counts infrastructure attempts only (worker lost, checkout failed). A nonzero exit or a timeout is an outcome and is never retried.

idempotency_key.description: Submitting the same key twice returns the first task id.

labels.description: Provenance, opaque to the queue: goal, experiment, task, submitted_by.

verify.description: Check each timed run's certificate in a separate process after its timing stops. The result carries runs[].verification and a top-level verification rollup; the task status is unchanged. Consumers treat refuted as an invalid measurement, never as a negative result, and error as unverified.

builtin.description: taskq.verify: independent recompute of discrete_log certificates over prime and binary fields.

argv.description: A verifier in the checkout; exit 0 verified, 1 refuted, 2 no claim. Gets TASKQ_CERTIFICATE and TASKQ_OUTPUT_DIR.
